Class VanillaScreenPanelAdapter

java.lang.Object
com.trevlar.menukit.api.panel.VanillaScreenPanelAdapter
public final class VanillaScreenPanelAdapter extends Object
Puts a Panel on vanilla non-container screens: Options, Controls, KeyBinds, world select, the title screen, and any other Screen that is not a container screen. The sibling of ScreenPanelAdapter; both declare into ScreenPanelRegistry, which builds one host per open screen. 
Panel panel = Panel.builder("mymod:options-help")
        .add(...)
        .position(PanelPosition.screenAnchor(InsideRegion.TOP_RIGHT))
        .build();
new VanillaScreenPanelAdapter(panel, 0).on(OptionsScreen.class);

Placement is the panel's

A non-container screen has no frame, so the panel declares screenAnchor(InsideRegion) (4px in from the edges it touches; siblings on one spot stack 4px apart), center(), or pixel(...). A region(...), main() or unplaced panel is rejected at construction.

Targeting is required

Call on(Class...) or onAny() exactly once. An adapter with no targeting fails loudly at the first screen open: an everywhere-default makes no sense across the title screen, Options and world select.

Input

The panel claims input by the one rule (PanelHost.claimsPoint(PanelHost.Placed, double, double)): an opaque panel its whole rectangle, a transparent one its solid elements. Vanilla widgets under a claim neither hover nor click.

Frozen after init

Construction, targeting and unregister() throw once MenuKit's declarations freeze at client start. Gate a panel at runtime with Panel.visibleWhen(BooleanSupplier).
